_comment: #3288 shrink-only ratchet for scripts/check-rls-route-coverage.mjs rule 2: per-file count of identity/credential-table statements that run on the bare pool with no RLS context, known, reviewed and NOT yet fixed. Lower a number when the route takes its read through a context helper (withAuthLookupContext / withAuthResolutionContext / withOAuthClientLookupContext / withTenantContext); raising it is a regression. Deleting this file sets every allowance to 0. An allowance for code that is actually correct is the failure mode this file has to guard against as much as a growth: #3315 deleted the three cron entries once rule 2 learned that sweepTenants pins a connection and sets app.current_tenant/app.current_user, because a tolerated finding is a ratchet that stops being evidence. Every entry needs a reason in _reasons (BASELINE_UNREASONED).

_reasons.app/api/scim/v2/Users/route.ts|PREAUTH_U: #3303. Made visible by rule 2's chain fusion: these five statements (`SELECT count(*)` and the paginated directory read at :122/:132, the pre-provisioning lookups at :230/:239, the read-back at :325) all sit on the bare pool behind `verifySCIMToken`, which authenticates an HMAC over `tenantId:expiry` and never opens an RLS context — so `users_read_self`/`users_tenant_member_read`, which derive the tenant from `app.current_user`, answer zero rows and a provisioned IdP is told the directory is empty. Counted, not fixed, because the fix is a privilege decision this guard must not make alone: either a `users_tenant_scim_read` policy arm keyed on a new `app.scim_tenant` GUC, or a super-admin `withSecurityContext` scoped to the request. Lower these two numbers when SCIM takes either.
_reasons.app/api/scim/v2/Users/[id]/route.ts|PREA: #3303. The same fusion surfaces the per-resource reads (:130 GET, :208 POST existence, :329 e-mail conflict, :397 PATCH read-back, :468 DELETE/PUT lookup), all on the pool with only `verifySCIMToken` in front of them, so `PATCH`/`DELETE` match zero rows and the IdP is told a user is deactivated while nothing is. Same two options as the collection route and the same reason for counting rather than waving: the choice between a machine-token policy arm and an escalated request context belongs to the owner of the SCIM privilege, not to a CI screen.
